title: Putting the Pieces Together: Self-Leadership
coreMove: Self-leadership guides managers, firefighters, and exiles as protectors, not enemies, so accountability can grow without shame running the system.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A case note about Joan, Brian, and childhood sexual abuse could become blame or a map of protection.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a clinician tracing a harmful episode to a protective part without excusing it.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Richard Schwartz's vocabulary can either become labels or a working map of exiles, managers, firefighters, and Self.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the full IFS role map to make a conflicted pattern workable.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A manager part can masquerade as excellence while using control, criticism, and vigilance to prevent old pain from surfacing.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show control becoming a clue to protection rather than a trait to praise blindly.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Nancy Shadick's rheumatoid arthritis studies invite cautious attention to psychological safety and immune functioning.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Keep the medical claim cautious while refusing to split body from inner safety.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Firefighters may use rage or self-destructive behavior when exiled pain breaks through, but repair still has to happen.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Start after the reactive episode and show protection plus repair.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Joan and Brian's IFS work shows that parts patterns live between people, not only inside one partner.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Turn a blame cycle into a parts map that preserves responsibility.
